import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Unfriendly partition conjecture

An *unfriendly partition* (or *majority colouring*) of a graph is a partition of its vertex set
into disjoint subsets such that every vertex has at least as many neighbours in the other subsets
as it has in its own subset. Every finite graph has one (a maximum cut into two parts), and
Shelah and Milner showed that every graph has an unfriendly partition into three subsets, while
an uncountable graph need not have one into two subsets.

The unfriendly partition conjecture asks whether every countable graph has an unfriendly
partition into two subsets.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Unfriendly partition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/unfriendly_partition)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in
  mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [AMP90] Aharoni, R., Milner, E. C., Prikry, K. (1990). "Unfriendly partitions of a graph."
  *J. Combin. Theory Ser. B* 50, pp. 1--10.
* [SM90] Shelah, S., Milner, E. C. (1990). "Graphs with no unfriendly partitions."
  In *A tribute to Paul Erdős*, Cambridge Univ. Press, pp. 373--384.
-/

open Cardinal

namespace UnfriendlyPartitionConjecture

variable {V ι : Type*}

/--
A colouring `c : V → ι` of the vertices of a graph `G` (equivalently, the partition of the vertex
set into the colour classes `c ⁻¹' {i}`, some of which may be empty) is an *unfriendly partition*
of `G` if every vertex `v` has at least as many neighbours in colour classes other than its own
as it has in its own colour class. The numbers of neighbours are compared as cardinals, so that
the definition is meaningful for vertices of infinite degree.
-/
def IsUnfriendlyPartition (G : SimpleGraph V) (c : V → ι) : Prop :=
  ∀ v, #(G.neighborSet v ∩ {w | c w = c v} : Set V) ≤
    #(G.neighborSet v ∩ {w | c w ≠ c v} : Set V)

/--
**Unfriendly partition conjecture.** Does every countable graph have an unfriendly partition
into two parts?

That is, for every simple graph $G$ on a countable (finite or countably infinite) vertex set,
is there a colouring of the vertices with two colours such that every vertex has at least as many
neighbours of the other colour as it has of its own colour (with the numbers of neighbours of a
vertex of infinite degree compared as cardinals)?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem unfriendly_partition_conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ {V : Type*} [Countable V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ c : V → Fin 2, IsUnfriendlyPartition G c := by
  sorry

/-- In a graph with no edges every colouring is an unfriendly partition. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isUnfriendlyPartition_bot (c : V → ι) :
    IsUnfriendlyPartition (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) c := by
  simp [IsUnfriendlyPartition, SimpleGraph.neighborSet]

/-- Giving the two vertices of a single edge different colours is an unfriendly partition. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isUnfriendlyPartition_top_fin_two_id :
    IsUnfriendlyPartition (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) id := by
  simp [IsUnfriendlyPartition]

/-- Giving the two vertices of a single edge the same colour is not an unfriendly partition. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isUnfriendlyPartition_top_fin_two_const :
    ¬ IsUnfriendlyPartition (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) (fun _ ↦ (0 : Fin 2)) := by
  simp [IsUnfriendlyPartition]

/--
Every finite graph has an unfriendly partition into two parts: a maximum cut is one, since a
vertex with more neighbours on its own side could be moved to the other side, increasing the
number of cut edges.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 5]
theorem exists_isUnfriendlyPartition_of_finite [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    ∃ c : V → Fin 2, IsUnfriendlyPartition G c := by
  sorry

/--
Every countable graph with only finitely many vertices of infinite degree has an unfriendly
partition into two parts [AMP90].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem unfriendly_partition_conjecture.variants.finite_infinite_degree [Countable V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : {v | (G.neighborSet v).Infinite}.Finite) :
    ∃ c : V → Fin 2, IsUnfriendlyPartition G c := by
  sorry

/--
Every countable graph in which every vertex has infinite degree has an unfriendly partition
into two parts [AMP90].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem unfriendly_partition_conjecture.variants.all_infinite_degree [Countable V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : ∀ v, (G.neighborSet v).Infinite) :
    ∃ c : V → Fin 2, IsUnfriendlyPartition G c := by
  sorry

/-- Every graph has an unfriendly partition into three parts [SM90]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem unfriendly_partition_conjecture.variants.three_parts (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    ∃ c : V → Fin 3, IsUnfriendlyPartition G c := by
  sorry

/--
There is an (uncountable) graph with no unfriendly partition into two parts [SM90].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem unfriendly_partition_conjecture.variants.not_two_parts :
    ∃ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), ¬ ∃ c : V → Fin 2, IsUnfriendlyPartition G c := by
  sorry

end UnfriendlyPartitionConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition matches the list entry; the note's requirements (countable = finite or countably infinite, cardinal comparison for infinite degrees, solved special cases and Shelah–Milner results not part of the slot) were all followed.
modeling_decisions: A 'partition into two parts' is modelled as a colouring `c : V → Fin 2` (parts `c ⁻¹' {0}`, `c ⁻¹' {1}`); parts may be empty. Requiring both parts nonempty would make the conjecture trivially false on a one-vertex graph, and the literature (Aharoni–Milner–Prikry, Shelah–Milner) uses 2-colourings.

'Countable graph' is modelled as a `SimpleGraph V` with `[Countable V]`, i.e. finite or countably infinite vertex set (Mathlib's `Countable` includes finite types). The edge set is then automatically countable.

The unfriendly condition compares, for each vertex v, `#(N(v) ∩ {w | c w = c v})` and `#(N(v) ∩ {w | c w ≠ c v})` as `Cardinal`s rather than `Set.encard`/`Finset.card`. For countable graphs `Set.encard` would be equivalent, but `Cardinal.mk` makes the bespoke definition correct for graphs of every cardinality (relevant to the Shelah–Milner results quoted in the article).

The definition `IsUnfriendlyPartition` is stated for an arbitrary colour type `ι` (every vertex has at least as many neighbours in *other* classes combined as in its own class), exactly following the Wikipedia definition; the slot uses `ι = Fin 2`.
The slot theorem quantifies `∀ {V : Type*}` inside the statement, making it universe polymorphic (as in `SidorenkoConjecture.lean`).

The definition lives in the problem file (under `UnfriendlyPartitionConjecture`) rather than `FormalConjecturesForMathlib` because only the candidate file may be written; it is applied as `IsUnfriendlyPartition G c` since dot notation does not resolve through the problem namespace.

Extra, clearly separated declarations were added beyond the slot: three provable `category test` lemmas for the new definition, a `category textbook` statement that finite graphs always have an unfriendly 2-partition (max-cut argument), and four `category research solved` variants taken from the article: countable graphs with finitely many infinite-degree vertices (AMP90), countable graphs with all degrees infinite (AMP90), unfriendly 3-partitions for every graph (SM90), and existence of a graph with no unfriendly 2-partition (SM90). The two AMP90 variants are deliberately restricted to countable graphs, matching the article's phrasing 'Among countable graphs ...'. The 'no end' and 'no subdivision of an infinite clique' special cases were not formalized (Mathlib lacks ends/rays/subdivision primitives), and they are not part of the slot.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: `SimpleGraph.Coloring` (proper colourings only — not applicable, an unfriendly partition need not be proper); `SimpleGraph.degree`/`neighborFinset` (finite only, would misstate infinite degrees); `SimpleGraph.edegree` in FormalConjecturesForMathlib (ℕ∞-valued total degree, does not split neighbours by colour and collapses all infinite cardinals); `Finpartition`/`Setoid.IsPartition` (no neighbour-count condition, and Finpartition is finite).
new_definitions.name: UnfriendlyPartitionConjecture.IsUnfriendlyPartition
new_definitions.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib has a notion of unfriendly partition / majority colouring, or of comparing the number of neighbours of a vertex inside vs. outside its own colour class as cardinals. `IsUnfriendlyPartition G c := ∀ v, #(G.neighborSet v ∩ {w | c w = c v}) ≤ #(G.neighborSet v ∩ {w | c w ≠ c v})`.

unfriendly_partition_conjecture.why: Stated as `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ {V : Type*} [Countable V] (G : SimpleGraph V), ∃ c : V → Fin 2, IsUnfriendlyPartition G c`, where the bespoke predicate `IsUnfriendlyPartition G c` says every vertex has at least as many neighbours of a different colour as of its own colour, with neighbour sets compared via `Cardinal.mk`. `answer(True)` corresponds to the answer 'yes'. `Countable V` covers finite and countably infinite vertex sets; parts of the partition may be empty (as in the literature's 2-colouring formulation).

Does every countable simple graph have a partition of its vertices into two parts such that,
for every vertex, the cardinality of its neighbors in the other part is at least the cardinality

Represented the two parts by a coloring `V → Fin 2`. No surjectivity is required: an unfriendly partition is conventionally a two-color assignment, and either part may be empty.

Expanded the definition of unfriendly inline: at each vertex, same-color adjacent vertices and opposite-color adjacent vertices form two subtypes, and the former's cardinality is at most the latter's.
Used `Cardinal.mk` rather than `Finset.card` or a natural-valued degree, so vertices of infinite degree are handled by genuine cardinal comparison.
Preserved the source's yes/no wording with `answer(sorry) ↔` followed by the universally quantified positive assertion.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The unfriendly partition conjecture

An *unfriendly partition* (or *majority colouring*) of a graph is a partition of its vertex set
into disjoint parts such that every vertex has at least as many neighbours in the other parts as
in its own part. Every finite graph has an unfriendly partition into two parts (a maximum cut is
one). Cowan and Emerson conjectured that every infinite graph has an unfriendly partition into two
parts; Shelah and Milner disproved this for uncountable graphs (and showed that three parts always
suffice). The case of countable graphs remains open.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia: Unfriendly partition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/unfriendly_partition)
* [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* R. Aharoni, E. C. Milner, K. Prikry, *Unfriendly partitions of a graph*,
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 50 (1990), 1--10.
* S. Shelah, E. C. Milner, *Graphs with no unfriendly partitions*, in *A tribute to Paul Erdős*,
  Cambridge University Press (1990), 373--384.
-/

open Cardinal

namespace UnfriendlyPartitionConjecture

variable {V ι : Type*}

/-- A colouring `c : V → ι` of the vertices of a graph `G` (i.e. a partition of `V` into the
fibres of `c`) is an **unfriendly partition** (or *majority colouring*) if every vertex `v` has
at least as many neighbours of a colour different from `c v` as neighbours of colour `c v`.
Vertices may have infinite degree, so the two sets of neighbours are compared as cardinals. -/
def _root_.SimpleGraph.IsUnfriendlyPartition (G : SimpleGraph V) (c : V → ι) : Prop :=
  ∀ v, #{w // G.Adj v w ∧ c w = c v} ≤ #{w // G.Adj v w ∧ c w ≠ c v}

/-- In the graph without edges, every colouring is an unfriendly partition. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isUnfriendlyPartition_bot (c : V → ι) :
    (⊥ : SimpleGraph V).IsUnfriendlyPartition c := by
  simp [SimpleGraph.IsUnfriendlyPartition]

/-- Colouring the two vertices of $K_2$ with different colours is an unfriendly partition. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isUnfriendlyPartition_top_fin_two_id :
    (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).IsUnfriendlyPartition id := by
  intro v
  simp only [SimpleGraph.top_adj, ne_eq, id_eq, mk_fintype, Nat.cast_le]
  fin_cases v <;> decide

/-- Colouring the two vertices of $K_2$ with the same colour is not an unfriendly partition. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isUnfriendlyPartition_top_fin_two_const :
    ¬ (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).IsUnfriendlyPartition (fun _ => (0 : Fin 2)) := by
  intro h
  have := h 0
  simp at this

/-- **The unfriendly partition conjecture.** Does every countable graph have an unfriendly
partition into two parts? That is, for every simple graph `G` on a countable (finite or countably
infinite) vertex set, is there a `2`-colouring of the vertices such that every vertex has at
least as many neighbours of the other colour as neighbours of its own colour? -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem unfriendly_partition_conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (V : Type*) [Countable V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ c : V → Fin 2, G.IsUnfriendlyPartition c := by
  sorry

end UnfriendlyPartitionConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single slot matches the list entry exactly, and its notes (countable = finite or countably infinite, cardinal comparison for infinite degrees, no additional variants) are the correct reading of the source.
modeling_decisions: 'Graph' is modelled as `SimpleGraph V` (no loops or multiple edges), the standard setting of Aharoni–Milner–Prikry and Shelah–Milner.

'Countable graph' is modelled as `[Countable V]` on the vertex type (finite or countably infinite); the edge set of a simple graph on a countable vertex set is then automatically countable. The vertex type is universe-polymorphic (`Type*`), following existing files such as `CernyConjecture.lean`.

'Partition into two parts' is modelled as a colouring `c : V → Fin 2` whose parts are the fibres of `c`; parts are allowed to be empty, as in the literature's definition via 2-colourings. Requiring both parts nonempty would make the one-vertex graph a trivial counterexample and is otherwise immaterial (an unfriendly colouring with an empty part forces the graph to be edgeless, in which case every colouring is unfriendly).

'At least as many neighbours in other sets as in its own set' is the non-strict inequality `#{same-colour neighbours} ≤ #{other-colour neighbours}` compared as `Cardinal`s, so vertices of infinite degree are handled correctly (not via `Finset.card`/`degree`, which need local finiteness).
The question form is kept: `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ...`, so `answer(True)` asserts every countable graph has a two-part unfriendly partition and `answer(False)` asserts a countable counterexample exists.

Per the decomposition notes, the solved special cases (finite graphs, finitely many infinite-degree vertices, rayless graphs, no infinite-clique subdivision) and the Shelah–Milner uncountable/three-part results are mentioned only in the module docstring and not stated as theorems. AMS tag 5 (Combinatorics) is used.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: `SimpleGraph.degree`/`SimpleGraph.neighborFinset` (require `LocallyFinite`, so cannot handle infinite degrees), `SimpleGraph.Coloring` (requires proper colourings, wrong notion), `Set.encard`/`Set.ncard` (encard would be faithful for countable graphs only since it collapses all infinite cardinalities to ⊤; `Cardinal.mk` was chosen so the definition is also correct for uncountable graphs), and Mathlib's `Combinatorics/Optimization/ValuedCSP` (only mentions max-cut in a docstring, no usable definition).
new_definitions.name: SimpleGraph.IsUnfriendlyPartition
new_definitions.why_needed: Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib have no notion of unfriendly partition / majority colouring (searched for `unfriendly`, `majority`, `MaxCut`). The predicate `∀ v, #{w // G.Adj v w ∧ c w = c v} ≤ #{w // G.Adj v w ∧ c w ≠ c v}` for a colouring `c : V → ι` is needed to state the conjecture; it is defined for an arbitrary colour type ι so that the two-part conjecture is the instance ι = Fin 2 (and the Shelah–Milner three-part result would be ι = Fin 3). Declared as `_root_.SimpleGraph.IsUnfriendlyPartition` inside the problem namespace so that dot notation `G.IsUnfriendlyPartition c` works. Three `@[category test]` lemmas with short proofs check it (edgeless graph: every colouring works; K₂ with a proper colouring: works; K₂ with a constant colouring: fails).

This is exactly 'every countable graph has an unfriendly partition into two parts', with infinite degrees compared as cardinals.

such that every vertex has at least as many neighbours in the other parts as in its own part.

unfriendly partition conjecture asks whether every countable graph has an unfriendly partition

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Unfriendly partition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/unfriendly_partition)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)

namespace UnfriendlyPartitionConjecture

open Cardinal

variable {V ι : Type*}

/--
A colouring `c : V → ι` of the vertices of a graph `G` (equivalently, the partition of the
vertex set into the fibres of `c`) is *unfriendly* if every vertex `v` has at least as many
neighbours in the other parts (i.e. of a colour different from `c v`) as in its own part
(i.e. of colour `c v`).

The two sets of neighbours are compared as cardinals, so that the condition also makes sense for
vertices of infinite degree.
-/
def IsUnfriendlyPartition (G : SimpleGraph V) (c : V → ι) : Prop :=
  ∀ v, #{w | G.Adj v w ∧ c w = c v} ≤ #{w | G.Adj v w ∧ c w ≠ c v}

/-- Every colouring of the edgeless graph is unfriendly. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isUnfriendlyPartition_bot (c : V → ι) : IsUnfriendlyPartition (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) c := by
  simp [IsUnfriendlyPartition]

/-- A constant colouring of a graph with at least one edge is never unfriendly. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isUnfriendlyPartition_const {G : SimpleGraph V} {v w : V} (h : G.Adj v w) (i : ι) :
    ¬ IsUnfriendlyPartition G (fun _ ↦ i) := by
  intro H
  have := H v
  simp only [ne_eq, not_true_eq_false, and_false, Set.setOf_false, mk_emptyCollection,
    nonpos_iff_eq_zero, mk_emptyCollection_iff, Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem,
    Set.mem_setOf_eq, and_true] at this
  exact this w h

/--
For a vertex `v` of finite degree, the unfriendliness condition at `v` is the usual comparison
of the numbers of neighbours of `v` of the same colour and of a different colour.
-/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isUnfriendlyPartition_iff_of_locallyFinite [DecidableEq ι] {G : SimpleGraph V}
    [G.LocallyFinite] (c : V → ι) :
    IsUnfriendlyPartition G c ↔ ∀ v, ((G.neighborFinset v).filter fun w ↦ c w = c v).card ≤
      ((G.neighborFinset v).filter fun w ↦ c w ≠ c v).card := by
  have key : ∀ (v : V) (p : V → Prop) [DecidablePred p],
      #{w | G.Adj v w ∧ p w} = ((G.neighborFinset v).filter p).card := by
    intro v p _
    have : {w | G.Adj v w ∧ p w} = ↑((G.neighborFinset v).filter p) := by
      ext w
      simp
    rw [this, Finset.coe_sort_coe, mk_coe_finset]
  simp only [IsUnfriendlyPartition, key, Nat.cast_le]

/-- Colouring the two vertices of the complete graph on `Fin 2` with different colours is
unfriendly. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isUnfriendlyPartition_completeGraph_fin_two :
    IsUnfriendlyPartition (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) (id : Fin 2 → Fin 2) := by
  rw [isUnfriendlyPartition_iff_of_locallyFinite]
  decide

/--
**The unfriendly partition conjecture.**
Does every countable graph have an unfriendly partition into two parts?

That is, for every simple graph $G$ on a countable (finite or countably infinite) vertex set, is
there a $2$-colouring of the vertices such that every vertex has at least as many neighbours of
the other colour as of its own colour, where the numbers of neighbours are compared as cardinals?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem unfriendly_partition_conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (V : Type) [Countable V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ c : V → Fin 2, IsUnfriendlyPartition G c := by
  sorry

/--
Every finite graph has an unfriendly partition into two parts: a maximum cut is one, since
otherwise a vertex with more neighbours in its own part could be moved to the other part,
increasing the number of cut edges.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 5]
theorem unfriendly_partition_conjecture.variants.finite [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    ∃ c : V → Fin 2, IsUnfriendlyPartition G c := by
  sorry

/--
Every countable graph with only finitely many vertices of infinite degree has an unfriendly
partition into two parts. This case is known to hold; see the Wikipedia article and
Aharoni, Milner and Prikry (1990).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem unfriendly_partition_conjecture.variants.finite_infinite_degree [Countable V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (h : {v | (G.neighborSet v).Infinite}.Finite) :
    ∃ c : V → Fin 2, IsUnfriendlyPartition G c := by
  sorry

/--
Every countable graph in which all vertices have infinite degree has an unfriendly partition
into two parts, by a back-and-forth argument. This case is known to hold; see the Wikipedia
article and Aharoni, Milner and Prikry (1990).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem unfriendly_partition_conjecture.variants.all_infinite_degree [Countable V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (h : ∀ v, (G.neighborSet v).Infinite) :
    ∃ c : V → Fin 2, IsUnfriendlyPartition G c := by
  sorry

/--
Cowan and Emerson conjectured that every infinite graph has an unfriendly partition into two
parts. Shelah and Milner (1990) disproved this: there is an (uncountable) graph with no
unfriendly partition into two parts.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem unfriendly_partition_conjecture.variants.exists_no_two_parts :
    ∃ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), ¬ ∃ c : V → Fin 2, IsUnfriendlyPartition G c := by
  sorry

/--
Every graph has an unfriendly partition into three parts (Shelah and Milner, 1990).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem unfriendly_partition_conjecture.variants.three_parts (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    ∃ c : V → Fin 3, IsUnfriendlyPartition G c := by
  sorry

end UnfriendlyPartitionConjecture

modeling_decisions: "Graph" is read as a simple graph (`SimpleGraph V`): undirected, loopless, no multiple edges. This is the standard meaning in the article and in the cited literature.

"Countable graph" is modelled as `[Countable V]` on the vertex type, so finite and countably infinite graphs are both included (the edge set of such a graph is automatically countable). An "unfriendly partition into two parts" is modelled as a 2-colouring `c : V → Fin 2` (parts = fibres of `c`). The definition is stated for an arbitrary colour type `ι` so that the same predicate serves the 2-part conjecture and the 3-part Shelah–Milner variant; "neighbours in other sets" is `c w ≠ c v`, i.e. all other parts combined, as in the article's definition.

The rayless and no-infinite-clique-subdivision cases were deliberately omitted because they would need new definitions (ends/rays, topological minors) with higher misformalization risk. API/test lemmas are included for the bespoke definition: every colouring of `⊥` is unfriendly; a constant colouring of a graph with an edge is not unfriendly; on a locally finite graph the predicate is equivalent to the usual `Finset.card` comparison of same-colour vs different-colour neighbours; and the 2-colouring of `K₂` is unfriendly (proved by `decide` through that equivalence).

/-!
# Unfriendly partition conjecture

An *unfriendly partition* (or *majority colouring*) of a graph is a partition of its vertex set
such that every vertex has at least as many neighbours in the other parts as in its own part.
For a finite graph a maximum cut is automatically an unfriendly partition into two parts.

Cowan and Emerson conjectured that every infinite graph has an unfriendly partition into two
parts. Shelah and Milner disproved this for uncountable graphs, but showed that an unfriendly
partition into three parts always exists. The unfriendly partition conjecture asks whether every
countable graph has an unfriendly partition into two parts. This remains open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Unfriendly partition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/unfriendly_partition)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [R. Aharoni, E. C. Milner, K. Prikry, *Unfriendly partitions of a graph*, J. Combin. Theory
  Ser. B 50 (1990), 1–10](https://doi.org/10.1016/0095-8956(90)90092-E)
- [S. Shelah, E. C. Milner, *Graphs with no unfriendly partitions*, in: A tribute to Paul Erdős,
  Cambridge University Press (1990), 373–384](https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511983917.031)
-/

namespace UnfriendlyPartitionConjecture

open Cardinal SimpleGraph

variable {V : Type*}

/-- A partition of the vertex set of `G` into two parts, encoded as a $2$-colouring
`c : V → Fin 2`, is *unfriendly* if every vertex has at least as many neighbours of the other
colour as neighbours of its own colour. The two numbers of neighbours are compared as cardinals,
so that vertices of infinite degree are handled correctly. -/
def IsUnfriendlyColoring (G : SimpleGraph V) (c : V → Fin 2) : Prop :=
  ∀ v, #{w ∈ G.neighborSet v | c w = c v} ≤ #{w ∈ G.neighborSet v | c w ≠ c v}

/-- Every $2$-colouring of the edgeless graph is unfriendly. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isUnfriendlyColoring_bot (c : V → Fin 2) : IsUnfriendlyColoring ⊥ c := by
  simp [IsUnfriendlyColoring]

/-- Colouring the two vertices of a single edge with different colours is unfriendly. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isUnfriendlyColoring_top_fin_two : IsUnfriendlyColoring (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) id := by
  intro v
  have : {w ∈ (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).neighborSet v | id w = id v} = ∅ := by
    ext w
    simp [eq_comm]
  rw [this]
  simp

/-- Colouring the two vertices of a single edge with the same colour is not unfriendly. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isUnfriendlyColoring_top_fin_two_const :
    ¬ IsUnfriendlyColoring (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) (fun _ => 0) := by
  intro h
  have h0 := h 0
  have h1 : {w ∈ (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).neighborSet 0 | (fun _ => (0 : Fin 2)) w = 0} =
      {1} := by
    ext w
    fin_cases w <;> simp
  have h2 : {w ∈ (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).neighborSet 0 | (fun _ => (0 : Fin 2)) w ≠ 0} =
      ∅ := by
    ext w
    simp
  rw [h1, h2] at h0
  simp at h0

/-- Every finite graph has an unfriendly partition into two parts: a maximum cut is unfriendly,
since otherwise moving a vertex with more neighbours in its own part to the other part would
increase the number of cut edges. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 5]
theorem exists_isUnfriendlyColoring_of_finite [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    ∃ c : V → Fin 2, IsUnfriendlyColoring G c := by
  sorry

/-- **Unfriendly partition conjecture.** Does every countable graph have an unfriendly partition
into two parts? That is, for every simple graph $G$ on a countable (finite or countably infinite)
vertex set, is there a $2$-colouring of the vertices such that every vertex has at least as many
neighbours of the other colour as neighbours of its own colour, where the numbers of neighbours
are compared as cardinals? -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem unfriendly_partition_conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (V : Type*) [Countable V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ c : V → Fin 2, IsUnfriendlyColoring G c := by
  sorry

end UnfriendlyPartitionConjecture

modeling_decisions: 'Graph' is taken to mean a simple graph (`SimpleGraph V`), the standard setting of the unfriendly-partition literature (Aharoni–Milner–Prikry, Shelah–Milner).

'Partition into two parts' is encoded as a 2-colouring `c : V → Fin 2`; parts are allowed to be empty. This agrees with the literature's 2-colouring formulation and avoids making the statement fail trivially on the empty or one-vertex graph; for any graph with at least one edge, an unfriendly colouring automatically has both parts nonempty.

'At least as many neighbours in other sets as in its own set' is formalised as `#{w ∈ G.neighborSet v | c w = c v} ≤ #{w ∈ G.neighborSet v | c w ≠ c v}` with `Cardinal.mk` (non-strict inequality), not `Finset.card`/`degree`, so vertices of infinite degree are treated correctly (a vertex of infinite degree needs infinitely many neighbours of the other colour, but may also have infinitely many of its own colour).

'Countable' is Mathlib's `Countable V`, which includes finite vertex types (the slot notes ask for finite or countably infinite); this does not change the truth value since finite graphs always have unfriendly partitions.

The vertex type is quantified over an arbitrary universe (`Type*`) inside the statement; since all countable types are in bijection with subsets of ℕ, this is mathematically equivalent to using `Type`.
The yes/no form of the list entry is rendered with `answer(sorry) ↔ …`, so `answer(True)` is the positive answer and all quantifiers come after the `answer`.

As an additional special case explicitly mentioned by the article (maximum cuts of finite graphs), the file also includes a sorry'd `@[category textbook]` statement `exists_isUnfriendlyColoring_of_finite` that every finite graph has an unfriendly 2-colouring; this is not a slot.
